heroHeadline: Junta Airstrike Kills 6 Civilians Including 3 Children in Palaw Township; SAC Three-Column Advance on Maw Taung Continues — Day 1,932
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,932 of Myanmar's civil war (May 18, 2026), Myanmar military junta forces conducted an airstrike in Palaw Township, Tanintharyi Region, killing six civilians — including three children (two 11-year-old boys and a 6-year-old girl) — according to the Karen National Union (KNU). The Palaw Township strike is the latest in an expanding SAC aerial campaign across southern Tanintharyi as junta forces press their three-column offensive toward Maw Taung, KNLA Brigade 4's critical Thailand border crossing, with SAC columns maintaining their position approximately 15 miles from the town while conducting daily airstrikes in support. Thousands of civilians continue to flee the Tanintharyi border zone toward Thailand as the junta offensive — now in its third day — shows no signs of pausing. The killing of three children in Palaw Township on May 18 brings the documented child-casualty death toll from Myanmar junta airstrikes in May 2026 alone to at least 27: following the May 7 Kyauktaw school bombing (19 students killed) and May 1 Khawpuichhip village strike (5 children ages 3–10). The UN's IIMM documented May 16 that at least 640 airstrikes have killed or injured children since the 2021 coup. Elsewhere, the Arakan Army and allied resistance maintain their assault on the junta's Nat Yay Kan hilltop strategic base in Padan Township, Magway Region, while SAC forces in Kani Township (Sagaing Region) continue ground operations displacing 30,900+ civilians from 44 villages. Myanmar's conflict remains at maximum breaking-news status as junta forces prosecute simultaneous multi-front offensives across Tanintharyi, Karen State, Sagaing, Magway, and Chin State.
footerNote: Data sourced from AAPP, ACLED, UN OCHA, Irrawaddy, RFA, Myanmar Now, DVB, Al Jazeera, Mizzima, Human Rights Watch, Crisis Group, Myanmar Peace Monitor, MoeMaKa CDM News, IMNA / Mon News Agency, CPJ, Narinjara News, Global Arakan Network, Kachin Human Rights Watch, Aryan Age, NUG Ministry of Human Rights, Committee to Protect Journalists, Chin People's Union and Army (CPU/A), Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK (BROUK), IIMM (UN Independent Investigative Mechanism for Myanmar), and official NUG, KNU, KIA, AA, and PDF statements.
